title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is upside down in the scan. It is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page '-10-' of an English typescript on linear algebraic groups, reused or filed among the 1965 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' notes. The neighbouring pages are Grothendieck's French manuscript on CM fields and Weil q-numbers. Reference [8] is almost certainly Chevalley's Séminaire 'Classification des groupes de Lie algébriques' (1956–58); its page numbering of the form 3-01, 6-15, 17-02 fits. The numbering (2.7–2.10), the style and the PSL(2) example strongly suggest a preprint of R. Steinberg, most likely 'Endomorphisms of linear algebraic groups' (Mem. AMS 80, 1968). An alternative is the related Springer–Steinberg material on centralizers of semisimple elements; I cannot confirm which.

The mathematics, step by step:
- Setting: G is a connected reductive (semisimple) group of rank r, and x is a semisimple element. Proposition 2.7 is stated on the previous typescript page; its tail is here. (a) The identity component of the centralizer is G_{x0} = G'T'. Here G' is semisimple, T' is a torus, G'∩T' is finite, and rank G' + rank T' = r. G' and T' are uniquely determined as the commutator subgroup of G_{x0} and the identity component of its centre. (b) All unipotent elements of the centralizer G_x lie in G'.
- Proof of (b) from (a): G_{x0} contains all unipotent elements of G_x.
- Proof of (a): put x in a maximal torus T. By uniqueness in the Bruhat decomposition y = u σ_w b, the three factors of any y in G_x again centralize x.
- 2.8: G_x is generated by T, the root subgroups X_α with α(x)=1, and the Weyl representatives σ_w with wx=x. G_{x0} is generated by T and those X_α alone. G' is generated by the X_α alone. T' is the identity component of the intersection of ker α over the roots with α(x)=1.
- 2.9 Corollary: every maximal torus containing x contains T'.
- 2.10 Remark: G_x can be disconnected even for regular x. Example: G = PSL(2) and x = image of diag(i,−i). The Weyl element [[0,1],[−1,0]] sends x to −x, which is the same element in PSL(2), so it centralizes x without lying in the torus.

These are the standard structure facts on centralizers of semisimple elements, the groundwork for Steinberg's connectedness theorem in the simply connected case. They have no direct mathematical tie to the CM / Weil-number computations on the surrounding Grothendieck pages. The most such a page could serve there is background on reductive groups (e.g. the motivic Galois group G(q) built from Weil q-numbers in L ⊂ Q'(i)).
errors: No mathematical errors. The example in 2.10 needs characteristic ≠ 2, which is implicit since i ≠ −i is required. 'imbed' is the typescript's own spelling.

ideas.what: Structure of the identity component of the centralizer of a semisimple element: G_{x0} = G'·T' (semisimple part times central torus), generated by T and the root subgroups with α(x)=1; the full G_x also needs the Weyl elements fixing x
ideas.modern_name: Centralizers of semisimple elements in reductive groups (pseudo-Levi / reductive centralizer structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Borel, Chevalley, Steinberg (Steinberg, Endomorphisms of linear algebraic groups, 1968; Springer–Steinberg, Conjugacy classes, LNM 131, 1970)
ideas.where_published: Steinberg Mem. AMS 80 (1968); Springer–Steinberg LNM 131; also SGA3 for general reductive group theory

ideas.what: Non-connectedness of the centralizer of a regular semisimple element in PSL(2) (x = diag(i,−i))
ideas.modern_name: Component group of centralizers / failure of Steinberg's connectedness theorem for non-simply-connected groups
ideas.where_published: Steinberg 1968; Springer–Steinberg 1970; Humphreys, Conjugacy Classes in Semisimple Algebraic Groups

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of someone else's typescript (almost certainly Steinberg) on standard centralizer theory, filed among Grothendieck's motivic-Galois notes. It has no Grothendieck content and nothing absent from the literature. At most it shows archivally that he had such a preprint at hand.
transcription_corrections: The page is scanned upside down; the transcription correctly reads it rotated.
The first line continues a sentence from the previous typescript page (probably '...G' and T' are closed connected subgroups with G_{x0} = G'T'...'); it is not a separate statement.
The original typescript spells 'imbed'; the transcription's 'imbed' is faithful.
